proposals.rationale: Default model provider mapping check looks up the wrong key: it checks the default provider against the model registry's mapping keyed by the wrong container, so a default model lacking a mapping for the default provider is checked against catalog providers instead and is accepted.

proposals.risk: a result its requirement or criteria name is computed or chosen wrongly
proposals.rationale: Required base URL validation only applies to providers that are in the catalog and skips the check when a provider is missing from provider_base_urls only if it is not the default provider; effectively a provider requiring a base URL is not rejected unless it is the default provider.

proposals.risk: one input partition its requirement or criteria name is no longer handled as they say
proposals.rationale: Optional policy limits are guarded by truthiness instead of `is not None`, so an explicit 0 for max_attempts or attempt_timeout_seconds skips validation and is accepted, even though 0 is invalid.

proposals.risk: an order or a before/after boundary its requirement names is broken
proposals.rationale: Default model provider mapping is checked before the default model is verified to exist in the registry, so an unknown default model raises a raw KeyError instead of the public ConfigurationError.

proposals.risk: an order or a before/after boundary its requirement names is broken
proposals.rationale: Attempt timeout and fallback-shuffle validation are nested under the 'max_attempts is not None' branch, so they are skipped whenever the route-attempt limit is unset and invalid values pass through to execution.

proposals.risk: an external interaction its requirement rules out happens anyway
proposals.rationale: Required base URL validation only applies to the default provider, so a config missing a base URL for another provider that requires one passes validation and can later trigger provider execution.
